contribution.note: Formalization of a published dependency for existing repository results, including general finite-choice and arithmetic adapters. No new open conjecture is claimed solved.
contribution.reference: J. Barajas and O. Serra, The lonely runner with seven runners, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 15 (2008), R48, doi:10.37236/772, Lemma 2 and Corollary 3

scope: Universal prime filtering with exact valuation levels and forbidden-set budgets, actual prime-power units, canonical p-adic maximum, full higher-residue preservation, the seeded folded-distance form of Barajas-Serra Corollary 3, and actual real-time loneliness consequences. The prime-seven consequence requires at most three distinct inputs at every valuation level strictly below the canonical maximum; the highest level is unrestricted. The uniform-level case has no cardinality cap and needs only a base at least two. These are proved input classes and reductions; the full six-speed runner theorem and its exceptional four/five-input lower levels are not claimed.
